clue.text: Bird of prey hunting dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hawk-like raptor that quarters open ground
second meaning: a breed of hound used for hunting hares

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one creature hunting another, but it is two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers both a raptor of the genus Circus and a hare-coursing hound breed.

clue.text: Patronised and irritable in South Atlantic?

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: in places the word for irritable inside the word for the Atlantic

parts.note: the Pond is a jokey name for the Atlantic Ocean
sore can mean irritated or touchy

explanation.surface: Someone feels patronised and touchy while far out in the South Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pond is jokey slang for the Atlantic. 'Patronised' here means backed financially, not talked down to.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise a cause or event is to support it with money, which is what sponsoring is.

clue.text: Good one about female artist's heavenly pair?

indicators.note: about here means the one goes round beside the artist, coming after her name

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British female artist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A query about a good artwork showing a celestial pair by a woman painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist known for confessional work such as her unmade bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Twins, Castor and Pollux, is a pair of figures in the night sky.

clue.text: Some work of Restoration in theatre?

definitions.text: Some work of Restoration in theatre?

parts.words: Some work of Restoration in theatre?
parts.note: suggests a Restoration play on stage, but means cosmetic restoring done in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Restoration' and 'theatre' point to seventeenth-century drama; the theatre is really a surgical one, and the restoration is to a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery tightening facial skin restores a youthful look and is performed in an operating room.

clue.text: How this answer should be written? Completely!

definitions.text: How this answer should be written?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a down entry, it is written vertically in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is self-referential: every down answer is entered vertically, starting at the upper square.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for thoroughly, as in searching a house in every part.

clue.text: Restrict unruly animals in Yosemite?

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of restrict are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to confine badly behaved wildlife in a US national park.
explanation.walkthrough: Yosemite is a US national park; the definition hints at American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is American colloquial for creatures, so beasts in a US park fit the question mark.

clue.text: Northern city has the advantage we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: someone who leads is ahead and so has the advantage

explanation.surface: A report that a city in the north is ahead of its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a major city in West Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Disaster if a rule broken

indicators.note: a rule broken is smashed apart, so its letters with if and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a regulation will lead to catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete flop or fiasco can be called a disaster, as in a play that bombed.

clue.text: Hoarder's representative that is collecting silver

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the representative holds the silver

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A collector's agent who is amassing silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the hoarder is the representative and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famed for picking up shiny objects, so a person who hoards trinkets is named after it.

clue.text: Cook may use this, as it happens, in nutty olio

indicators.note: in puts the word for as it happens inside the scrambled letters
nutty means crazy, so the letters of olio are scrambled

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A cook may use this, as it happens, in a mixed stew flavoured with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: An olio is a spicy stew or hotchpotch; 'nutty' looks like a flavour but is the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed fruit fat is a standard cooking fat for frying and dressings in a kitchen.

clue.text: Yankee in crimson reformed Old Boy network

indicators.note: in places the Yankee letter inside the reshuffled letters
reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters of crimson are rearranged

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American in red, now reformed, joins the old school-tie circle.
explanation.walkthrough: An Old Boy is a former pupil of a British school; the network is favouritism among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring friends and old school contacts for jobs is the practice of appointing pals.

clue.text: Time magazine's absorbing material

parts.note: an issue is a single edition of a magazine

explanation.surface: Time magazine has gripping content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time magazine' looks like the news weekly, and 'absorbing' looks like gripping, but the definition is soft paper that soaks things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft paper used for blowing noses or mopping spills soaks up liquid.

clue.text: Love child for one backed First Nations leader

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a minor is a child in law
e.g., for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A love child, for example, supported a Native leader.
explanation.walkthrough: OMINOREG read backwards gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an Apache war chief who resisted US and Mexican forces in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: A thin person must stop fit winger

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so A RAKE fills the middle of the word for fit

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or temper
a rake is a very thin person, as in thin as a rake

explanation.surface: A skinny player has to block a fit wide forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the wing, but here it is anything with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-tailed parrot is a bird, and so a creature with wings.

clue.text: Take on PM playing around with mistress?

indicators.note: playing around means fooling about, so the letters of take on PM and the with letter are mixed up

explanation.surface: Taking on a Prime Minister who fools around with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman supported financially by a lover she is not married to is a paramour.

clue.text: Appropriate vehicle parts hired again?

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the vehicle pushes the hired-again word open

parts.note: to relet is to let out on hire again
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Suitable car components rented out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun for vehicle components, but it is a verb: the van separates RELET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent to the matter in hand is fitting, the adjective sense here.

clue.text: Depart with singer Shaw for Californian port

parts.note: Sandie Shaw is an English pop singer who won Eurovision in 1967
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Leaving with a pop star for a harbour city in California.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandie Shaw was a 1960s British pop singer, famous for singing barefoot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large harbour city in southern California, near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Completely self-obsessed king breaks fast?

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: breaks means bursts into, so the king goes inside the self-obsessed word

parts.note: ego suggests self-obsession, as in an ego trip
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A totally vain monarch ends his period of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a period without food, but it is a musical tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian tempo marking means brisk and lively, so it signals a quick pace.

clue.text: It protects new snake and duck having trouble

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so it wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Something guards a fresh snake and a duck that are struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a difficult situation or predicament, stuck with no easy way out.

clue.text: For Bryn Terfel say stick with one note?

parts.note: a bar is a rod or stick
one is I, the Roman numeral, and a note is a tone in music

explanation.surface: For a famous Welsh opera singer, perhaps, keeping to one note.
explanation.walkthrough: Bryn Terfel is a Welsh opera singer with a deep male voice. TONE comes from 'note' as a synonym, not by rearranging its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a bass-baritone, and 'say' marks him as an example of a male voice type.

clue.text: Seldom right, a bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A financial institution that is seldom correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun for a lender, but it is a verb: to bank on, to rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning not often, infrequently.

clue.text: Old saw that's lost its edge?

definitions.text: Old saw that's lost its edge?

parts.words: Old saw that's lost its edge?
parts.note: suggests a blunt tool, but a saw is also a saying, and one worn out by overuse

explanation.walkthrough: A saw is an old saying as well as a cutting tool; a saying that has lost its edge is stale.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed expression used so often it has lost its force is a stale, trite phrase.

clue.text: End is near

definitions.meaning: second meaning: nearby, said with a hard s

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a doom-laden warning; the two words are separate meanings, and they are pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a finish or conclusion; as an adjective it means at a short distance.

clue.text: Tories to suspect one not sticking neck out?

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or unreliable, so the letters of Tories to are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Conservatives distrust a politician who keeps a low profile and never takes risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticking neck out' looks like taking a risk, but it is meant literally: a reptile pulling its head into its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled reptile withdraws its head into its shell, so literally it keeps its head in.

clue.text: I allow small number inside in the dark

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for number within the word for allow

parts.note: to grant is to allow
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone permits a few things in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed, lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Field with flower in Yorkshire — take me there!

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Don runs through Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A meadow with blossoms in the Yorkshire countryside makes someone ask to be taken there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows; the Don flows through Sheffield and Doncaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal command is said to a guide asking them to go ahead and show the way.

clue.text: Lefties' second letter to Greeks returned

definitions.note: the possessive stands for the name of a left-wing Labour group, a noun

parts.note: a second is a moment

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the Greek letter is written backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A left-wingers' second letter to the Greeks came back.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is a left-wing campaign group within Britain's Labour Party; the clue reads 'Lefties' (group) is ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaigning organisation founded in 2015 to back Jeremy Corbyn is a group of socialists.
